selected.title: The Sticking Point Journal
selected.audienceGap: Students feel overwhelmed by the choice and think they are failing to 'just know' the answer.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Recognizes that confusion is a data point for research, not a sign of poor fit.
selected.concept: Two students share their notes on a simple task and realize their confusion points are different.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Students feel comfortable documenting specific uncertainties.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A simple task of organizing a budget for a school event.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Budgeting. Sticking point: Categorizing expenses.
demonstration.observation: Student finds that their specific confusion is the best place to start asking for help.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Where can I find a breakdown of how budgets are audited?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / three_column_audit; Connection = task_question_journal / peer_observation_journal; Discovery = insufficient_information / missing_evidence_reveal. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

hlni.insight: A short illustrative task reveals specific confusion points that guide targeted research, rather than serving as an aptitude test.
hlni.audienceGap: Students believe they must 'know' which degree fits them inherently.
hlni.viewerChange: Students shift from guessing to asking specific, research-based questions.
hlni.support: Using a task-based observation creates data points for research that are specific to the student's current level of understanding.
hlni.payoff: The student produces a concrete, investigable question that replaces general anxiety.

creativeAngle: Using a task-based journal to turn confusion into actionable research questions.
objective: Help students move from feeling stuck to identifying specific areas for further research.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Choosing Dilemma
shots.visual: A student looking at brochures for B.Com and BBA with a worried expression.
shots.dialogue: Stuck between B.Com and BBA? Stop guessing.

shots.name: The Confusion Point
shots.visual: Student holds a pen, staring at a blank notebook.
shots.dialogue: Don't pick a degree yet. Compare the work.

shots.name: The Worksheet Reveal
shots.visual: Student writes on a piece of paper labeled 'Budgeting Task'.
shots.dialogue: Try a task and map your sticking points.

shots.name: The Insight Delivery
shots.visual: Close up of the paper showing: 'Example: Task: Budgeting. Sticking point: Categorizing expenses.'
shots.dialogue: This isn't a test. Find your knowledge gaps.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Budgeting. Sticking point: Categorizing expenses.
shots.cameraPerformance: Macro shot focusing on the handwriting.

shots.name: The Better Question
shots.visual: Student writes: 'Where can I find a breakdown of how budgets are audited?'
shots.dialogue: Now ask: 'Where can I find a breakdown of how budgets are audited?'
shots.onscreenText: Where can I find a breakdown of how budgets are audited?

shots.name: The Final Action
shots.visual: Student closes the notebook and looks at the camera confidently.
shots.dialogue: Use this to investigate course teams directly.
